scope_discipline_when_reporting_what_a_s.title: Scope discipline when reporting what a specific function returns
scope_discipline_when_reporting_what_a_s.content:
When a task asks what a specific named function returns (as opposed to what a subsystem effectively resolves), restrict the answer to that function's own control flow and return statements. Sibling helpers in the same file that consult additional sources (ambient credentials, fallback config, OS lookups) are out of scope unless the target function calls them on the path to its return value.

Before answering, explicitly enumerate the target function's return paths, including hardcoded early-return branches, not just the main table/map lookup. Members with no matching branch and no table entry return undefined and should be reported as such (or omitted, if the task says omit).

prime_agent_getapikeyenvvars_structure_i.title: prime-agent: getApiKeyEnvVars structure in packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts
prime_agent_getapikeyenvvars_structure_i.content:
In prime-agent (verified at v0.7.0), `getApiKeyEnvVars(provider)` in `packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts` has a very simple shape:

1. Two hardcoded special cases returning multi-element arrays, in this order:
   - `github-copilot` -> ["COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"]
   - `anthropic` -> ["ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]
2. A single lookup into a flat `const envMap: Record<string, string>` literal; a hit returns a one-element array `[envMap[provider]]`.
3. Anything absent from both returns `undefined`.

Of the 32 members of the `KnownProvider` union in `packages/ai/src/types.ts`, only `amazon-bedrock` and `openai-codex` are absent from envMap, so those two return `undefined` (they are OAuth/ambient-credential providers).

Important scoping gotcha: ambient credential sources are NOT part of `getApiKeyEnvVars`'s return value. `AWS_*` variables and `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` are read elsewhere in the same file (inside `getEnvApiKey` and `hasVertexAdcCredentials`). Do not fold them into getApiKeyEnvVars results.

Duplicate env var values exist in envMap: `moonshotai` and `moonshotai-cn` both -> MOONSHOT_API_KEY; `opencode` and `opencode-go` both -> OPENCODE_API_KEY; `cloudflare-workers-ai` and `cloudflare-ai-gateway` both -> CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY. Also note `google` -> GEMINI_API_KEY and `google-vertex` -> GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY (not GOOGLE_*_API_KEY naming you might guess).

Because the file also lazily imports node:fs/os/path via `dynamicImport` to stay browser/Vite safe, never convert those to top-level imports when editing it.

prime_agent_getapikeyenvvars_verified_re.title: prime-agent v0.7.0: verified getApiKeyEnvVars result matrix (30 of 32 providers)
prime_agent_getapikeyenvvars_verified_re.content:
Verified result of `getApiKeyEnvVars(provider)` in packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts for every member of `KnownProvider` (packages/ai/src/types.ts), prime-agent v0.7.0 at /home/bench/work/repo. Confirmed twice by direct source read.

Counts: `KnownProvider` has 32 members; the flat `envMap: Record<string, string>` literal has 28 pairs; 2 special-case `if` branches precede the lookup. Non-undefined returns: 30 providers. Returns undefined (omit from any output object): `amazon-bedrock`, `openai-codex` — these are absent from both special cases and envMap because their credentials are AWS-ambient / OAuth-only, handled in `getEnvApiKey` and `hasVertexAdcCredentials`, NOT in `getApiKeyEnvVars`.

Multi-element returns (the only two, both from hardcoded special cases, order matters):
- github-copilot -> ["COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN", "GH_TOKEN", "GITHUB_TOKEN"]
- anthropic -> ["ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]

Single-element returns via envMap (source order of the union, each value wrapped in a 1-element array):
google->GEMINI_API_KEY; google-vertex->GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY; openai->OPENAI_API_KEY; azure-openai-responses->AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY; prime-inference->PRIME_API_KEY; deepseek->DEEPSEEK_API_KEY; xai->XAI_API_KEY; groq->GROQ_API_KEY; cerebras->CEREBRAS_API_KEY; openrouter->OPENROUTER_API_KEY; vercel-ai-gateway->AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY; zai->ZAI_API_KEY; mistral->MISTRAL_API_KEY; minimax->MINIMAX_API_KEY; minimax-cn->MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY; moonshotai->MOONSHOT_API_KEY; moonshotai-cn->MOONSHOT_API_KEY; huggingface->HF_TOKEN; fireworks->FIREWORKS_API_KEY; opencode->OPENCODE_API_KEY; opencode-go->OPENCODE_API_KEY; kimi-coding->KIMI_API_KEY; cloudflare-workers-ai->CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY; cloudflare-ai-gateway->CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY; xiaomi->XIAOMI_API_KEY; xiaomi-token-plan-cn->XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_CN_API_KEY; xiaomi-token-plan-ams->XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_AMS_API_KEY; xiaomi-token-plan-sgp->XIAOMI_TOKEN_PLAN_SGP_API_KEY.

Gotcha: env var values are NOT unique per provider — MOONSHOT_API_KEY (moonshotai, moonshotai-cn), OPENCODE_API_KEY (opencode, opencode-go), and CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY (cloudflare-workers-ai, cloudflare-ai-gateway) each appear twice. Never dedupe by value.

Fast re-derivation (both regexes worked first try):
  union = re.search(r'export type KnownProvider =(.*?);', types, re.S).group(1)
  providers = re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', union)              # 32
  block = re.search(r'const envMap: Record<string, string> = \{(.*?)\n\t\};', src, re.S).group(1)
  pairs = re.findall(r'"?([\w\-]+)"?:\s*"([A-Z0-9_]+)"', block)   # 28, source order preserved
Hyphenated provider ids appear as quoted keys in envMap but the optional-quote regex above handles both forms.

extract_typescript_union_members_and_str.title: Extract TypeScript union members and string-map literals from source
extract_typescript_union_members_and_str.content:
Static extraction helper for answering "what does this TS lookup return for every member of this union?" style questions without an AST toolchain.

Why it exists: in the prime-agent env-api-keys task, the fastest correct path was to read whole files into Python and regex two things: (1) the members of an exported union type alias, and (2) the key/value pairs of a `Record<string, string>` object literal. Then join them and diff to find the members with no entry (which return undefined).

Usage pattern:

```python
from prime_skills.ts_extract import ts_union_members, ts_string_map, join_union_to_map

members = await ts_union_members(path="packages/ai/src/types.ts", type_name="KnownProvider")
env_map = await ts_string_map(path="packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts", const_name="envMap")
mapped, missing = await join_union_to_map(members, env_map)
```

- `ts_union_members` regexes `export type <Name> =(.*?);` then pulls every double-quoted literal, preserving source order.
- `ts_string_map` regexes `const <Name>: Record<string, string> = {...};` then pulls `"?key"?: "VALUE"` pairs, preserving source order and tolerating quoted hyphenated keys.
- `join_union_to_map` returns `(dict_of_hits, list_of_members_absent_from_map)`.

Caveats that matter for correctness:
- Regex extraction only covers the literal map. Hardcoded `if` special-case branches above the lookup must be read by eye and merged manually; a map-only answer will silently omit them.
- Verify the union member count against the source before trusting downstream results.
- Always confirm the enclosing function's scope: sibling functions in the same file may read additional env vars that are NOT part of the target function's return value.

Call each entry point natively as `await <callable>(...)`.

path.description: Absolute or repo-relative path to the .ts file to read.

type_name.description: Name of the exported union type alias to extract members from (used by ts_union_members). Required for ts_union_members.

const_name.description: Name of the object-literal const to extract key/value pairs from (used by ts_string_map). Required for ts_string_map.

preserve_order.description: Keep source declaration order in returned members and map pairs.
